newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Prospect of Cyprus talks improving, says UN envoy.
newsitem.headline: Prospect of Cyprus talks improving, says UN envoy.

text.p: Prospects are improving for the resumption of direct talks between Greek and Turkish Cypriots by June, the U.N. envoy in divided Cyprus said on Friday.
"I think we are getting closer," said Gustave Feissel, resident representative of the U.N. secretary-general in Cyprus.

"Of course until we get there...it doesn't matter if you are 95 percent near the goal, you have to be 100 percent and that is what we are trying to achieve," he added after meeting President Glafcos Clerides, the Greek Cypriot leader.
Amid growing tension, international pressure has been mounting for a solution to the decades-old Cyprus problem ahead of the possible start of talks on its joining the European Union.
International mediators expect a meeting between Clerides and Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash in June. It will be the first in almost three years.
U.N. special envoy Han Sung-joo, a former South Korean foreign minister, arrives on Saturday. He will attend meetings Feissel is scheduled to have with the two leaders next week.
A U.N. peacekeeping force has been stationed in Cyprus since 1963. The island has been divided since Turkey invaded its northern third in 1974 after a coup sponsored by Athens.

A small army of mediators has failed for decades to reunite Cyprus under a federal umbrella. The dispute remains a source of tension between NATO partners Greece and Turkey, guarantor powers of Cyprus along with former colonial ruler Britain.
The United Nations has been working on the adoption of goodwill gestures by both sides to improve the climate for talks, soured after ceasefire-line killings last year.
Cypriot government spokesman Manolis Christofides said Clerides has submitted proposals to the United Nations.
"The goal of rapproachement is the right one, and must be sought with more drastic and determined measures and means," Christophides said, without elaborating.
Neither side has disclosed proposed goodwill measures, abiding by a U.N. appeal for a media blackout.

Clerides is president of the administration in the south, internationally recognised as the island's legitimate government. Denktash heads a breakaway Turkish Cypriot state in the north recognised only by Ankara.
The 1,200-strong U.N. force patrols a buffer zone between some 30,000 mainland Turkish forces in northern Cyprus and 11,500 Greek Cypriot conscripts in the south.
